canonical_examples.problem:
Given that the minor of $a_{23}$ is $5,$ find all the possible values of $k$ in the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273095/assets/0b33ff00c054de07fbcf607be4fea299cfa56e977436ab87e0a6e916d629344b.svg)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we remove the second row and third column:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273095/assets/996d67bec102879d74afd3ea159b30fdb2792fe075f268a2327c8b1998c6dde0.svg)

The minor of $a_{23}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}det[\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ -1 & 2k\end{aligned}] & =|\begin{aligned}k & 3 \\ -1 & 2k\end{aligned}| \\  & =k\cdot 2k-3\cdot (-1) \\  & =2{k}^{2}+3.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the minor of $a_{23}$ is $5,$ so we must have:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{k}^{2}+3 & =5 \\ 2{k}^{2} & =2 \\ {k}^{2} & =1 \\ k & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $k=-1$ and $k=1.$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
The **minor** of the entry $a_{ij}$ in a matrix $A$ is the determinant of the remaining entries when the row and column containing $a_{ij}$ are removed.

For instance, suppose we want to find the minor of $a_{{\color{red}1}{\color{blue}2}} = {\bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{-1}}$ (row ${\color{red}1}$, column ${\color{blue}2}$) in the matrix $A$ given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273095/assets/49f34a9c0f1841cb6d2e96d1e7c896be9287b82d897b368365a8b1ad0ad22c9b.svg)

To find the minor, we exclude all entries in row $1$ and all entries in column $2\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273095/assets/a3b401e5887c314971a6eda145e5b0dabbc7039f5de2c235c82238bb70ee1657.svg)

This leaves us with the $2\times 2$ determinant given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273095/assets/d0475e4a8b54dd9e623c71fb5090f7125d30c504955bc7be1fdc1d61e4af5758.svg)
We call it $M_{{\color{red}{1}}{\color{blue}{2}}}$ to denote the fact that it was obtained by deleting row $\color{red}1$ and column $\color{blue}2$ of the matrix $A.$

Finally, we compute the above determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}5 & 7 \\ 8 & 4\end{aligned}| & =5\cdot 4-7\cdot 8 \\  & =20-56 \\  & =-36\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.content:
The **minor** of the entry $a_{ij}$ in a matrix $A$ is the determinant of the remaining entries when the row and column containing $a_{ij}$ are removed.

For instance, suppose we want to find the minor of $a_{{\color{red}1}{\color{blue}2}} = {\bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{-1}}$ (row ${\color{red}1}$, column ${\color{blue}2}$) in the matrix $A$ given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273095/assets/49f34a9c0f1841cb6d2e96d1e7c896be9287b82d897b368365a8b1ad0ad22c9b.svg)

To find the minor, we exclude all entries in row $1$ and all entries in column $2\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273095/assets/a3b401e5887c314971a6eda145e5b0dabbc7039f5de2c235c82238bb70ee1657.svg)

This leaves us with the $2\times 2$ determinant given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14273095/assets/d0475e4a8b54dd9e623c71fb5090f7125d30c504955bc7be1fdc1d61e4af5758.svg)
We call it $M_{{\color{red}{1}}{\color{blue}{2}}}$ to denote the fact that it was obtained by deleting row $\color{red}1$ and column $\color{blue}2$ of the matrix $A.$

Finally, we compute the above determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}5 & 7 \\ 8 & 4\end{aligned}| & =5\cdot 4-7\cdot 8 \\  & =20-56 \\  & =-36\end{aligned}
$$
